why_predeclared: the analysis is fixed now so that it cannot later be shaped by which mode produces the more convenient answer
background: DCSI is frozen as PAPER-faithful. A diagnostic variant, dcsi_author_compat, reproduces the author's multiclass routine, whose separation is exactly twice the published definition. The two modes rank candidates identically for K=2 but can rank them differently for K>=3, because the multiclass value is the mean of a nonlinear transform of q. The primary analysis therefore cannot simply assert mode-independence; it must be shown.

what_will_be_recomputed.quantity: every endpoint in which DCSI appears as a comparator, recomputed with sep_mode=AUTHOR_COMPAT and with everything else -- corpus, protocol, candidate bank, utility definition, tests -- held fixed
endpoints: per-index vs modern comparator pool tests
oracle_win_frequency where DCSI is the winning comparator

what_will_be_reported: the fraction of (dataset, view) units whose DCSI-based comparison changes sign
the fraction of K>=3 units, since K=2 units cannot change by construction
whether any BH-adjusted conclusion changes status at the frozen threshold

decision_rule.if_no_conclusion_changes: report the sensitivity analysis as a robustness check and keep the PAPER-mode result as primary
decision_rule.if_any_conclusion_changes: report BOTH modes side by side in the results, state plainly which conclusions are mode-dependent, and do not present the mode-dependent conclusion as established
decision_rule.what_is_never_permitted: selecting the mode that produces the preferred conclusion, or reporting only the mode that does

primary_result_definition_is_fixed_now: the PAPER mode is primary regardless of the sensitivity outcome, because it is what the paper defines and what the authors' own published values reproduce (validation/dcsi_published_value_reproduction.json). The sensitivity analysis can qualify a conclusion; it cannot promote the diagnostic variant to primary.
k_distribution_note: the frozen candidate bank (fixed32) contains K>=2 partitions; only the K>=3 subset can exhibit a mode-dependent ordering, so the size of that subset bounds the possible impact and will be reported alongside the result
